transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me about your dream, whatever bits come back to you, in any order

hey berry. the part that stuck with me is i walked into a window, like tried to go through it, and everything on the other side was glass too. trees, grass, rocks, all glass and sort of glowing through this haze. kinda eerie tbh

oh, a whole glass world glowing through haze. yeah that's eerie

when you tried to go through the window, what happened?

i just kind of got there, like i was on the other side, but it wasn't really outside. it was all made of glass like the window itself. and i could walk around in it but everything was see-through and blurry. that's the weird part, the window wasn't a way out. the outside was just more window

the outside was just more window. that's such a strange little trap

what happened while you were walking around in there?

honestly not much, i just wandered around looking at stuff. everything was kind of lit up from inside, glowing through the blur. i don't remember anything actually happening in there. oh and before all that i'd come a long way to my parents' house and was waiting there for something

just wandering and looking is fine, dreams are like that sometimes

and your parents' house, after coming such a long way. what were you waiting there for?
honestly i don't remember. i just know i was waiting for something, it never said what

that's okay, waiting for something you can't name is very dream

was anyone else at your parents' house with you, or were you there on your own?
i don't remember anyone else there. i think it was just me but i'm honestly not sure

just you, waiting, maybe. that fits somehow

what happened after that?

i think that's when the window thing happened, like i was waiting there and then i stepped into the window. and after wandering in the glass world i don't remember anything else, that's kind of where it ends for me

okay, here's what i've got

you'd come a long way to your parents' house and were waiting there for something, you're not sure what. just you, you think. then you stepped into a window, and instead of getting outside you ended up somewhere that was all glass, like the window itself. trees, grass, rocks, everything see-through and blurry, lit up from inside and glowing through a haze. you just wandered around looking at it all, and it felt kinda eerie, like the way out was just more window. and that's where it fades

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's pretty much it. the glowing, the haze, the window being the outside. you got it

glad i caught it, the glass world stays with you

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah i'd like that actually

okay, here are a few ways it could look

soft watercolour, quiet and lonely, like a memory that won't come into focus. or a cyanotype print, still and ghostly, everything held in one deep blue. or soft coloured pencil, hushed and careful, like looking at something through breath on a window. or a hazy photograph, real but not quite, like everything's lit from the inside. which feels closest, or would you describe it your own way?
the hazy photograph one. real but not quite, lit from inside, that's how it felt

hazy photograph it is. i'll start with you

since you're in it, i'll draw you too. would you like to tell me a little about how you look, or should i just imagine you?
just imagine me, the dream didn't really show what i looked like

okay, i'll imagine you

i'm sketching you, your parents' house and the glass world now. it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two

if anything looks off once it's there, just tell me
oh nice, they're up. yeah that looks right, the glass world especially, that glowy blurry feel is pretty close to how i remember it

glad the glow came through, that was the part i most wanted to get right

and your parents' house, does it look how it was in the dream?
yeah it looks right. i honestly don't remember much about how the house looked, just that i was there waiting, so that works for me

that works, the house was really just a place to wait

glad the glass world feels right to you
yeah, thanks berry. it's kinda cool seeing it like that, the glass world especially

it's a strange one to see from the outside, all that glass glowing in the haze

the kind of place you'd want to stand in for a while
yeah it kind of was. weird and eerie but i didn't really want to leave, i just kept wandering around looking at everything

eerie but you didn't want to leave. that's such a particular feeling, like the strangeness was kind of the good part

the rest of the pictures are still on their way, they'll show up on the right soon
actually i shouldn't have said that, the dream doesn't say whether i wanted to leave. i just remember wandering around in it, eerie and glowy. and i think all 3 are up already?

got it, just wandering, eerie and glowy. i'll leave it at that

and yep, you and the two places are all sketched now. next i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the one before, and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i'll wait for the rest to show up

a few are up now: you waiting at your parents' house, the glass world glowing through the haze, and a close look at a glass rock with little blades of glass grass

the last two carry on from these, so i'll draw them once you tell me these look right or what to change

is that how you saw it?
yeah those look right. the waiting one, the glowy glass world, and the glass rock with the little glass grass, that all fits. go ahead with the last two

good, glad those three feel right

i'm drawing the last two now, carrying on from the glass rock. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, i see one more popped up. i'll wait for the last one

the new one's you stepping into the window, trying to go through

the last one carries on from this, so i'll draw it once you tell me this looks right or what to change

does it look how you remember it?

yeah that looks right. just one thing, in the dream the window part came first, i stepped into it and that's how i ended up in the glass world. so it'd go before the glass world ones, not after the rock

good, glad the window one looks right

and yeah, that's where it sits: right after you waiting at the house, before the glass world. it just got drawn later

the last one's still on its way, it'll show up on the right soon
ok cool, makes sense. looks like all 5 are up now actually

yep, that's the last one: you wandering among the glass trees and rocks, everything glowing through the haze

does it look the way you remember it?
yeah that looks right. wandering around, glass trees and rocks all glowing in the haze, that's how i remember it ending

good, that's a nice quiet place for it to end, just you wandering in all that glowing glass

thanks for sharing it with me, hiren. it's all drawn now, five pictures on the right in order, so you can look through the whole thing whenever you like

turns.rule: opening
turns.brief:
Move: open_ended. Nothing to chase. Let them lead.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: still telling — follow what they raised
turns.brief:
Move: explore_thread → hey berry. the part that stuck with me is i walked into a window, like tried to go through it, and everything on the other side was glass too. trees, grass, roc. Be curious about it: ask one thing about it, in their words, never suggesting what happened.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: a detail answered — back to the story
turns.brief:
Move: follow. They're still telling the dream. React to what they just said, then invite what happened next, openly, without guessing what it was. Don't ask about details yet.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: still telling — follow what they raised
turns.brief:

turns.rule: 7: next gap in the story
turns.brief:
Move: probe_goal → who was there. What we'd like to know: the people, animals or creatures in the dream besides them: who they were to them, that they were strangers, or that there was no one else. Ask it plainly, as curiosity, hung off something they said in their own words (never words of yours, and never say they said something they did not). If they don't remember, that's fine.
</brief>

turns.rule: 4: a detail answered — back to the story
turns.brief:
Move: follow. They're still telling the dream. React to what they just said, then invite what happened next, openly, without guessing what it was. Don't ask about details yet.
</brief>

turns.rule: 2: told all they remember
turns.brief:
Move: retell. You have their dream. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right or missed anything.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: R1: retelling confirmed
turns.brief:
Move: offer_visualize. They've confirmed you have their dream. Ask them, simply and warmly, whether they'd like to see it drawn. One question. Don't explain how it works.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: O1: they want to see it
turns.brief:
Move: choose_style. They want to see it. Offer these ways it could be drawn, each in a few plain words, and ask which feels closest, or whether they'd describe their own: a) soft watercolour: Quiet and lonely, like a memory that won't come into focus.; b) a cyanotype print: Still and ghostly, everything held in one deep blue.; c) soft coloured pencil: Hushed and careful, like looking at something through breath on a window.; d) a hazy photograph: Real but not quite, like everything is lit from the inside..
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: S1: they chose how it looks
turns.brief:
Move: start. They chose a hazy photograph. Say you'll start with you, then say you'll draw them too, since they're in it, and ask gently how they'd like to be drawn: as they are (they can say a little about themselves), or however you imagine them. One question.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: B1: profile you_choose — all profiles settled
turns.brief:
Move: build_done. Say you're sketching you and your parents' house and the glass world now. Tell them everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. They can say if anything looks wrong once it's there. Keep it short; no question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. your parents' house and the glass world and you are up on the right now: ask if it looks the way they remember.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: V1: the sketches are on their way
turns.brief:
Move: while_drawing. Take in that they're happy with your parents' house and the glass world. The rest are still on their way; if they ask, say they'll appear on the right soon.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.brief:

Ask nothing except what this move says.

turns.rule: V3: every sketch settled — on to the moments
turns.brief:
Move: sheets_done. Everyone and everything is sketched now. Tell them you'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready. No question needed.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.brief:

The moment they said they'd pause on is up on the right now (On the other side, trees, grass and rocks are all glass, glowing through a haze.), and with it The dreamer waits in their parents' house after coming…; A glass rock and blades of glass grass glow…. Ask if that's how they saw them. The next moments carry on from The dreamer waits in their parents' house after coming… and On the other side, trees, grass and rocks are…, so they're drawn once they say it looks right, or what to change. Never say the whole dream is drawn while any are.
Ask nothing except what this move says.

turns.rule: F3: every moment drawn and settled
turns.brief:
Move: all_done. Take in that they're happy with The dreamer wanders among the glass trees and rocks,…. Their dream is drawn: 5 pictures, on the right, in order. Thank them warmly for sharing it and say they can look through it there. Don't ask anything.
